issues.title: Inter-mode emergence was overcharacterized

failure_location.quote: Within the scope of this general behavior, different training errors will lead to different normal and tangent motions, which can be quantified, and these detailed motions characterize when inter-mode generations emerge.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the directional motions characterize when inter-mode generations emerge. The old paper actually proves a conditional upper bound on E[||u||²] and gives an approximate local motion equation. Those results neither characterize the generated tangent-space distribution nor determine when positive probability appears between modes, so the claimed characterization materially exceeds the established support.
issues.overall_effect: The formal directional bounds remain usable, but they support only a partial explanatory mechanism rather than the advertised characterization of inter-mode emergence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the claim to say that the second-moment bound and approximate tangential SDE isolate one directional mechanism that can help explain structured intermediate generations, while explicitly disclaiming any characterization of the tangent-space distribution or determination of when inter-mode probability appears.
issues.why_classification: The phrase “characterize when” makes a coherent substantive promise that the old results do not establish. Qualifying it is local and leaves the formal bounds intact, but it meaningfully withdraws the distributional and onset characterization. Because a recognizably comparable partial-mechanism claim survives without new proof architecture, the issue is moderate.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Rather than fully characterizing the generated distribution within the tangent space, the slide analysis identifies a specific tangential motion that helps explain structured intermediate generations.

issues.title: Directional bounds used an undefined shared coefficient
issues.failure_explanation: Both conclusions contain an undefined C_delta. The supplied transfer theorem provides only the direction-specific factors C_delta^perp and C_delta^parallel, which must multiply the corresponding normal and tangent decompositions.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is literally ill-defined as printed, although its intended directional bounds are immediately recoverable and no later formal result depends on the malformed notation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace C_delta in the normal bound by C_delta^perp and C_delta in the tangential bound by C_delta^parallel.
issues.why_classification: The preceding transfer theorem defines exactly these two direction-specific coefficients, uniquely forcing the corresponding substitutions. No inference, proof step, hypothesis, rate, or downstream result changes, so this is a transcriptional defect.

issues.title: Early high-noise ridge distances lacked spectral reliability

failure_location.quote: \emph{Steps 0-200:} the process is dominated by pure Gaussian noise, resulting no distance-decay.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that Steps 0–200 constitute a normal-distance stage whose flat curve reflects Gaussian-noise dynamics. The old paper actually establishes that ∇²log p_t=-I/h_t+Σ(t,x)/h_t² with Σ formed from values a_t x0; consequently, the anisotropic eigengaps defining E collapse as a_t tends to zero, while the experiment supplies no gap threshold or failure check. Thus the early plotted statistic does not support the claimed normal-distance interpretation.
issues.overall_effect: The earliest MNIST points cannot reliably support the asserted ridge-distance stage. This affects the experimental scope, not the later-distance regime or any formal theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce and report a positive tangent-normal eigengap reliability threshold, treat the earliest high-noise measurements as unreliable when they fail it, and remove their interpretation as a normal ridge-distance stage. Restrict the experimental stage claim and plot interpretation to later points with reliable spectral separation.
issues.why_classification: The old Hessian formula shows that its anisotropic eigengaps collapse as a_t approaches zero, so the early statistic cannot retain its claimed ridge-distance meaning without a reliability check. The repair leaves later measurements and all formal results intact, but withdraws an advertised interpretation over the natural high-noise phase. That is a limited experimental-scope weakening rather than a same-guarantee minor correction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: we deliberately omit the initial high-noise stages at $t=10.0$ and $t=4.67$

issues.title: Ridge projection omitted curvature feasibility

failure_location.quote: Then we can only consider $F(x) = E(x)^\top \nabla \log p(x) = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimator treats the zero set of the normal score as the ridge, although Definition def:ridge also requires λ_{d*+1}≤-β. Thus it can accept a stationary point outside the ridge and report zero distance to the wrong set.
issues.overall_effect: The old MNIST procedure could report distance to the normal-stationarity set rather than distance to the defined ridge. The paper's formal ridge theorems do not depend on this numerical estimator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require every returned projection candidate y to satisfy both the normal-score tolerance and lambda_{d*+1}(y) <= -beta. A candidate failing the curvature test must produce an explicit failure rather than a ridge distance, and affected experimental summaries must be recomputed using only certified candidates.
issues.why_classification: The omitted inequality is part of the defining target set, not merely a numerical tolerance, and normal stationarity can hold at non-ridge points. A contained feasibility check yields a comparable certified estimator, but it can remove outputs previously promised on unrestricted inputs; preserving a total output would instead require a constrained projection construction. This is limited loss or contained nontrivial repair, hence moderate.

issues.title: Newton linearization omitted the eigenspace derivative

failure_location.quote: By neglecting high-order variations of the eigenvector field $E(x)$, we obtain:

issues.failure_explanation: Holding E fixed drops (DE[δ])^T∇log p, a first-order product-rule contribution. Unless E is locally constant or an additional cancellation is proved, the Hessian-only formula is not the Newton step for F and has no stated first-order accuracy as a ridge-distance estimator.
issues.overall_effect: The old experimental estimator could be systematically biased on curved or spatially rotating ridge geometries. The theoretical results based on the exact projection map are not dependent on this estimator.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Differentiate F(y)=E(y)^T grad log p(y) by the full product rule, using J(y)=E(y)^T Hess log p(y)+(nabla_y E(y))^T grad log p(y), compute the spectral-subspace derivative under an explicit eigengap condition, and use this Jacobian in the Newton linear solve. Recompute the experimental distances with the corrected solver.
issues.why_classification: The old derivation deliberately discards a generally first-order term, so the defect is not transcriptional. Recovering a genuine Newton step requires constructing and evaluating the eigenspace derivative and revalidating the numerical estimator. This is contained but nontrivial work; it preserves the intended experiment and does not affect the formal ridge theorems, so it is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Newton estimator used an unguarded spectral inverse

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To measure the distance from a point $x$ to $\mathcal{R}_{d^*}$

issues.failure_explanation: The step applies Λ_perp(x)^{-1} at an unrestricted trajectory point. Neither the ridge definition nor the estimator's input contract ensures that every selected eigenvalue at that point is bounded away from zero, so the computation can be undefined or arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical distance estimator is not well-defined on all inputs admitted by its old interface, although no formal theorem relies on it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the raw spectral inverse by a safeguarded solve: check a declared minimum eigenvalue magnitude or condition threshold, use a stated Tikhonov-damped solve when the threshold fails, and flag regularized values in the experimental diagnostics.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine well-definedness defect, but a standard local conditioning check and damped solve resolve it without a new lemma or algorithmic architecture. The original Newton formula and outputs are unchanged in the regular regime up to an immaterial numerical safeguard, and no formal theorem depends on the estimator; therefore the issue is minor rather than a typo or moderate issue.
